title: Runtime Patchloader for Live Kernel Fixes and Incremental ABI Hotpatching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We frequently discover small kernel- or launch-config-level issues (register pressure tweaks, launch bounds, quantization-specific math kernels) that require a full runtime restart or a new binary deployment to fix. These restarts are disruptive for Dedicated pools and complicate private deployments. Goal: introduce a controlled 'patchloader' subsystem that can deploy small, signed binary patches or micro-kernel overrides to the serving runtime at runtime without full service restarts. The system will be scoped to micro-kernels (<= 64 KB), have a strict verification step (signature + provenance), and include automatic rollback criteria tied to latency/accuracy telemetry. This ticket covers prototyping the loader, CI signing flow, a small on-disk patch format, and a canary rollout for a single problematic CUTLASS GEMM variant used by quantized 4-bit Llama variants.
acceptance_criteria: Loader can apply a micro-kernel override to a running runtime process without restarting worker processes
Applied patch must be verified (ED25519 signature) and rejected if verification fails
Canary rollout mechanism exists: patch applied to 1% of requests for a selected model, with telemetry gating
Automatic rollback triggers when 95th percentile latency increases > 10% or error-rate increases > 2x over baseline
End-to-end CI test demonstrates applying, verifying, and rolling back a patch in staging with no memory leaks or worker crashes
Documentation describing patch format, signing process, operator UX, and security restrictions is published in Confluence (link in comments)
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for patch application + signature verification. 2) Integration: apply patch to staging dedicated node running a canary model, validate correctness against golden outputs. 3) Load test: 30m steady load on patched node to detect memory/regression. 4) Fault injection: corrupted signature, truncated payload, and patch that intentionally triggers a kernel assert to validate rollback. 5) Long-run: 24h soak with telemetry collection (latency, error-rate, GPU utilization).
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only cluster (runtime-image: patchloader-alpha) - engineers can upload signed patches and observe effects
Beta: dedicated-staging with canary traffic (1% of requests) for one quantized Llama model
Canary evaluation window: 30 minutes with automated checks (latency, error-rate, output-diff on sampled prompts)
Progressive ramp to 10% then 50% if metrics stable, with manual approval for 100%
For Private/VPC customers: operator must opt-in; patches are applied only after customer grants signed-blob allowlist
risks: Incorrect patch could corrupt GPU state or cause silent numerical regressions
Complexity of safely unloading/replacing code paths that hold CUDA contexts
Security risk if signing keys are compromised; must integrate with KMS + key rotation
Compatibility: older Triton/CUTLASS combos may not expose patch points, requiring graceful fallback to full deploy
Operational burden: operators need clear UX and rollback hooks to avoid hand-holding during incidents
implementation_notes: Prototype approach: use a patch table of function entry points (registered by runtime at startup) and allow micro-kernel blobs to replace entries in the table. The loader will use dlopen-like semantics for our kernel registry and map patched code into a reserved memory region with page protections. We will avoid touching existing CUDA contexts where possible by routing through an indirection table. Security: sign blobs with ED25519 and enforce KMS-backed key management via the CI signing pipeline. Fallback: if patch application fails, loader leaves original pointers intact and records a failure event to Sentry/telemetry.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after postmortem for ENG-82345 where a CUTLASS bug required urgent worker restarts; proposal scoped and initial design doc drafted
2025-02-18: Spike complete - can load a 16KB blob and update indirection table in a single-process dev harness (repo: runtime/patchloader-spike)
2025-02-22: Security sync - decided on ED25519 for signing and KMS storage in the CI signing pipeline; security review requested
2025-02-26: Implemented basic verification and applied first non-functional patch in internal test cluster; observed no immediate regressions but some transient allocation spikes
2025-03-03: PR opened (runtime#2783) with loader core + unit tests; CI signature flow PR (ci-sig#47) added. Plan to run integration tests this week
review_feedback: Platform Eng: keep loader scope minimal to micro-kernels only and gate on patch size (< 64KB)
Security: require KMS-signed allowlist for private deployments; rotate signing keys quarterly
SRE: add explicit telemetry events for patch-apply, patch-reject, rollback-start, rollback-complete; expose in Console runbooks
ML infra: ensure sampled output comparisons (BLEU/embedding cosine) are part of canary checks for quality-sensitive models
notes_for_oncall: If a patch causes increased GPU OOMs or worker crashes: disable patch via control plane (patchloader-disable flag), run rollback, collect kernel logs (/var/log/runtime/patchloader.log), escalate to ENG-86109 on-call. Monitor per-model 95th / 99th percentile latency in Console and check error-rate dashboards.
